warnings ## How this fits together The embedded agent runner collects each tool’s terminal outcome, then turns the completed attempt into channel reply payloads. This change alters the final warning decision that follows model output and affects what channel users see after tool failures. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Model turn] --> B[Tool execution outcomes] B --> C[Terminal error observer] C --> D[Reply payload builder] D --> E{User-facing reply?} E -->|Yes| F[Assistant reply only] E -->|No and failure remains| G[Tool failure warning] F --> H[Channel delivery] G --> H ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should the default channel policy treat every user-facing assistant reply as authoritative after a failed write, send, or persistence operation? | **Adopt reply-authoritative warnings:** Merge the two-rule policy, accepting that terminal warnings are reserved for runs with no user-facing reply. | Why: This is an intentional default-product tradeoff between eliminating stale false-positive warnings and retaining a final corrective signal when model text incorrectly claims a side effect succeeded. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Merging intentionally removes the terminal warning after a user-facing reply even when a write, send, or persistence operation failed; a misleading reply can therefore be the only channel-visible outcome while failure details remain in progress and Control UI. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - A maintainer must choose the intended default warning semantics before this policy-changing refactor can land.
